question: Which of the following has deuterium as one of its isotopes?
solution:
The correct answer is** **__**Hydrogen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Deuterium is an isotope of hydrogen** which is composed of one electron, one proton and one neutron. 

 
 
• **Atomic Number of Deuterium** - **1.**
 
• **Mass number- 2.**
 
• **Symbol- 2H**.
 
• **Non radioactive** in nature.
 
• The nucleus of a deuterium atom is called a **deuteron**.
 
 
 
• [IMAGE: https://ars.els-cdn.com/content/image/3-s2.0-B9780128148532000011-f01-11-9780128148532.jpg] 
 
• **Uses of Deuteron**: 
 
 
• Deuterium is used **as liquid D₂O in heavy water moderated fission reactors**** to slow neutrons **without the high neutron absorption of ordinary hydrogen.
 
• Deuterium is most commonly used in hydrogen **nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy**.
 
• Deuterium is used as a non-radioactive, **stable isotopic tracer.**
 
• Deuteron is used in** Nuclear Weapons**.
 
• A **deuterated drug** is a small molecule medicinal product drugs significantly** lower rates of metabolism**.
 
• Deuterium used as **Thermostabilization**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• An **antideuteron** is the **antimatter counterpart of the nucleus of deuterium**, consisting of an antiproton and an antineutron.
 
• Other two Isotopes of Hydrogen are - **Tritium and Protium**.
